subsystems.name: Cold atom source
subsystems.role: produces the ultracold atoms that act as the interferometer's test masses.

subsystems.name: Atom optics
subsystems.role: laser pulses that split, redirect and recombine the atomic wavepacket, standing in for mirrors and beam splitters.

subsystems.name: Vacuum baseline
subsystems.role: lets the atoms fly freely for a large fraction of a second without collisions.

subsystems.name: Laser and frequency-control system
subsystems.role: keeps the interrogating laser phase-stable enough that a faint field-induced phase shift is not buried.

subsystems.name: Detection
subsystems.role: reads out the fraction of atoms in each output port, which encodes the interference phase.

subsystems.name: Noise suppression
subsystems.role: rejects vibration, gravity gradients and laser phase noise that mimic a real signal.

buildSteps.title: Cool and trap the atoms
buildSteps.detail: Laser cooling brings a gas of atoms to microkelvin temperatures, slow enough that their quantum wavelength is macroscopic.

buildSteps.title: Launch them along the tube
buildSteps.detail: An optical lattice or moving standing wave gives the cloud a controlled velocity so it travels down the baseline.

buildSteps.title: Split the wavepacket
buildSteps.detail: A first laser pulse puts each atom into a superposition of two different momenta — two arms of the interferometer in one cloud.

buildSteps.title: Hold over the baseline
buildSteps.detail: The two arms separate by tens to hundreds of metres and accumulate phase at slightly different rates for about a second.

buildSteps.title: Reverse the arms
buildSteps.detail: A second pulse flips the momentum difference so the arms begin to converge again.

buildSteps.title: Recombine
buildSteps.detail: A final pulse closes the interferometer; the phase difference shows up as a change in the relative population of two output states.

buildSteps.title: Read the fringe
buildSteps.detail: Imaging measures that population difference, the instrument's primary output.

buildSteps.title: Scan and correlate
buildSteps.detail: The measurement is repeated while varying the pulse spacing, sweeping candidate field frequencies; two separated interferometers are compared so local noise cancels.

prerequisites.tech: Laser cooling and cold atom sources
prerequisites.why: the atomic test masses must be colder than anything in nature for the interference to survive.

prerequisites.tech: High-power, narrow-linewidth lasers and frequency combs
prerequisites.why: phase noise in the interrogating light directly limits the detectable signal.

prerequisites.tech: Long high-vacuum tubes with magnetic shielding
prerequisites.why: baselines of 100 m and beyond are being built for longer free-fall times.
ground motion and Earth's gravity field otherwise dominate the interferometer phase.

prerequisites.tech: Ultralight dark matter and scalar-field theory
prerequisites.why: provides the predicted phase-versus-frequency patterns that the experiment looks for.

pathway.milestone: metre-scale atom gradiometers in operation; the 100 m MAGIS-100 instrument under construction at Fermilab and the staged AION programme in the UK
pathway.unlocks: demonstration that large-baseline atom interferometry works outside the laboratory.

pathway.milestone: 100 m instruments running continuously and networked with a second detector
pathway.unlocks: sensitivity to a first range of ultralight field couplings, with local noise rejected.
reach into the frequency band where ultralight dark matter is most plausible.

pathway.milestone: widely separated detector networks, and concepts for space baselines
pathway.unlocks: a genuine search instrument that can either find a signal or rule out a large swathe of theory.
